gui.description: Qt6 Widgets MIDAS verification GUI (apps/verification-gui) plus its Qt-independent verification/ library (ExcelReferenceReader, via xlnt for .xlsx); not built by default, requested only via -DVCPKG_MANIFEST_FEATURES=gui so the routine Ubuntu CI matrix in ci.yml never builds Qt6/xlnt from source. qtbase is requested with default-features:false + an explicit minimal {gui,widgets,thread} list ('core' is implicit, cannot be named) -- 'thread' confirmed necessary by reading Qt's own src/corelib/configure.cmake (QProcess's 'process' feature requires 'QT_FEATURE_thread OR NOT UNIX'). On Linux, qtbase additionally needs {xcb,xcb-sm,xcb-xlib,xrender} (platform-filtered, matching exactly the platform:linux entries in qtbase's OWN default-features list) -- without them vcpkg passes '-DINPUT_xcb=no' to Qt's build, so the QXcbIntegrationPlugin (libqxcb.so) simply never gets built at all, even though the required system X11/XCB -dev packages are installed; the GUI then fails to start with 'could not find the Qt platform plugin xcb' (GUI-7, 2026-10-21/22). windeployqt is requested only on Windows (platform-filtered), since it is a Windows-only deployment tool with no effect on Linux. Still excludes qtbase's heavier default-features that are genuinely unused here (dbus, sql-psql, sql-sqlite, testlib, icu, harfbuzz, brotli, network, opengl, openssl, async-io, sessionmanager, dnslookup, zstd), which is what was exhausting a GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runner's disk building them from source.
